gaps.quote: If $\lambda\le1$ the sum is at most $d$.
gaps.note: The sum 1+lambda+...+lambda^d has d+1 terms, each at most 1, so it is at most d+1, not d (at lambda=1 it equals d+1 > d). The paper (paper.tex lines 1555-1556) says 'at most k+1'. The conclusion O(mu^{d tau}) still holds, but the stated bound is wrong.

gaps.term: linear cost of outer two updates
gaps.quote: The outer two cost linear time.
gaps.note: The page never says that field D comes after H in tape order. The linear-time claim holds only because the outer updates change the later field using the earlier one (paper.tex lines 1347-1352 and 1520-1523, 'The other two updates target the later group'; Lemma matrix-shear needs every H_i before every D_j). Without this hypothesis the claim is unsupported.

The page never gives the value or a bound for mu for the explicit network and does not mark this as cited. The reader cannot check mu<2^20. The paper states it as a fact about the fixed network (paper.tex line 1333, 'Since m<2^20').

gaps.term: enough rows for splitting into streams
gaps.quote: Each smaller call acts on one of the $W$ [wire streams](role-streams.md), each of volume $V/W$.
gaps.note: The split into W streams of volume V/W, repeated at every depth, needs a row field preceding both chunks whose length is divisible by W^k (Proposition power-interchange, paper.tex lines 1481-1485). The page states no such hypothesis and presents the recursion for any array, so the recursion analysis is missing a hypothesis. The paper removes it by padding in the arbitrary-width lemma (lines 1631-1735), which the page does not mention.
